A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffuseSG research, with matching authors, core formulation, datasets, and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph-generation, graph-completion, image-generation, and SGTR data-augmentation results in Tables 1-4, with additional qualitative results in the supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation, completion, and SGTR experiments and adds baseline results, encoding/loss ablations, and conditional-image and relation-control evaluations in Tables 3-8.

M1.justification: V1 pairs DiffuseSG with pretrained LayoutDiffusion. V2 adds Relation-ControlNet, using Stable Diffusion V1.5 with object/relation spatial channels and relation-triplet text prompts to condition image generation on relations as well as layouts (Section 4.2.2). DiffuseSG's core architecture, encodings, losses, and sampler remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Visual Genome and COCO-Stuff remain the underlying datasets. V2 adds evaluations of object/relation fidelity in generated images and a distinct relation-control scenario requiring different semantic relations under matched object/layout conditions (Section 5.3). These extend task requirements beyond v1's generation, completion, and downstream detection evaluations.

E2.justification: SceneGraphGen and VarScene join BLT, LayoutDM, D3PM, and DiGress in the graph-generation comparison (v2 Table 3). New image-generator comparisons evaluate Relation-ControlNet against LayoutDiffusion and Object-ControlNet (Tables 6-7), substantially extending the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V1 matches validation node counts, including rejection sampling for LayoutDM. V2 separates fixed-count comparisons from DiffuseSG* comparisons that sample counts from the validation distribution. New image evaluations use MOTIFS-SUM-TDE classifiers, object and relation-balanced triplet accuracies, 5,000 VG graphs, and 328 matched/swapped triplets. VarScene's new COCO-Stuff results explicitly use undirected graphs. V1's VG-5033/COCO-Stuff-3097 FID protocol is removed.

E4.justification: V1 compares three encodings without IoU loss and tests adding IoU loss for binary encoding. V2 completes the encoding-by-IoU ablation with scalar and one-hot variants trained with IoU loss (Table 4). It also adds the Object-ControlNet conditioning ablation and matched/swapped-relation analysis, including a qualitative posture-control case study (Tables 6-7, Figure 6).

E5.justification: Image-generation replication disclosures change with the evaluations: v1 Appendix 8.1 specifies one image-sampling repetition on VG and five on COCO-Stuff, whereas v2 Section 5.3 specifies five images per VG graph or relation triplet. Both retain three generated sample sets for graph evaluation and four SGTR training runs. Neither reports seeds, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for new baselines, DiffuseSG*, expanded ablations, and conditional-image evaluations, while removing v1 Table 3's FID results. Retained results also change: VG D-MMD changes from 2.97e-3 to 5.26e-3 for DiffuseSG and from 4.45e-3 to 8.89e-3 for DiGress. LayoutDM's revised scores accompany a changed count-sampling protocol and are not same-setting gains. Completion and SGTR results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The substantive graph formalization, joint-distribution factorization, diffusion equations, losses, complexity argument, and appendix sampler are retained. V2 makes existing MMD and TV formulas explicit and rewrites F1 weighting equivalently. The terminology taxonomy and training pseudocode do not introduce new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 reframes novelty around a grounded scene graph-image framework and explicitly extends its comparative claim to unconditional scene-graph generators. The introduction also incorporates relation-aware image generation. The central claims about DiffuseSG's mixed-attribute generation, completion, and synthetic-data utility remain; 'grounded' clarifies the representation already generated in v1.

C2.justification: V2 discusses IoU loss failing with scalar/one-hot encodings and hypothesizes that binary-tuned hyperparameters explain this. It newly interprets relation conditioning's benefits on targeted tests alongside worse object accuracy and inferior full-VG performance, attributing limitations partly to relations predictable from layouts. These qualifications motivate retaining LayoutDiffusion downstream. V1's discussion of BLT's high FID and limited category coverage disappears with that experiment.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, explicit zero-based encoding details, and substantial ControlNet implementation information. Appendix A.4 specifies Stable Diffusion V1.5, optimizer parameters, learning rate 0.00001, 200 epochs, batch size 120, and prompt dropout. Appendix C.1 documents category filtering for image evaluation. Existing DiffuseSG architecture and sampler settings are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands related work with dedicated discussions of unconditional scene-graph generation and conditional image generation. It newly acknowledges Garg et al. (2021) and Verma et al. (2022), positioning DiffuseSG's inclusion of bounding boxes against their label-only graphs. Broader diffusion and image-generation literature is also added.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and contribution narrative, introduces a representation-taxonomy section, and systematically adopts 'grounded scene graph' terminology. Methods and experiments are reorganized into graph-generation and conditional-image-generation branches with additional subsection hierarchy; the supplement becomes Appendices A-D. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The two-column presentation becomes a single-column journal layout. V1's sampling illustration is replaced by a detailed training/network diagram; v2 adds ControlNet and downsampling/upsampling diagrams, taxonomy and capability tables, and relation-control imagery. Generation and ablation tables are separated, completion and SGTR tables are reformatted, and the old FID table is removed. Appendix qualitative examples are retained and reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's missing comparisons with directly related unconditional scene-graph generators and provides substantial evidence about the benefits and limits of relation-conditioned image generation. The fuller encoding/IoU ablation, explicit negative findings, clearer positioning, and added implementation/access information materially strengthen the paper. These gains outweigh removal of the original FID comparison and remaining comparison weaknesses: VarScene's COCO evaluation is undirected, and the VG D-MMD discussion incorrectly calls SceneGraphGen second-best when Table 3 places VarScene ahead of it.
